title: Privileged Access Forensic Playbook & Custodian Handoff Protocol
author: Anjali Desai
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the operational procedure for investigating incidents that involve privileged access (human or machine). It prescribes an end-to-end forensic evidence orchestration process, the responsibilities for custodianship handoff, minimal-impact evidence collection commands, data residency and retention constraints, RBAC remediation steps, and packaging guidance for compliance evidence requests. Intended audience: Incident responders, on-call SREs, Security Engineers, Legal, and Privacy.

Scope
-----
- Applies to incidents where elevated credentials were used or requested, including service accounts, short-lived role escalations (JIT), and operator consoles.
- Covers systems that produce authorization and audit artifacts: API Gateway, Identity Provider (IdP), service mesh, control plane audit store, model serving runtime, and storage buckets containing logs or artifacts.
- Excludes: low-risk non-privileged application errors unless they surface privileged token exposure.

Goals and success criteria
-------------------------
- Evidence collected within initial containment window (T+120 minutes) for high-severity privileged incidents.
- Chain-of-custody manifest generated and signed by custodian before evidence transfer.
- Audit log extracts validated to match sequence hashes and stored in immutable evidence bucket with documented retention period and access controls.

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Incident Commander (IC): Security on-call lead — overall decision authority.
- Forensic Custodian: Security engineer assigned to collect, validate, and steward evidence artifacts.
- SRE Custodian: Platform engineer responsible for extracting platform-side telemetry and ensuring chain-of-custody for compute/storage.
- Legal & Privacy Liaison: Reviews legal hold, cross-border data residency constraints, and external disclosure.
- App Owner: Eng owner for the impacted service; provides business context and assists with access attestations.

Immediate response checklist (first 0-30 minutes)
--------------------------------------------------
1. IC declares privileged-incident response and notifies Legal & Privacy Liaisons.
2. Set short-lived containment controls: block access token issuance for implicated role, mark service account keys as disabled (not deleted), apply temporary deny policies in control plane.
3. App Owner confirms whether elevated credentials were expected for recent runbooks/maintenance.
4. Assign Forensic Custodian and SRE Custodian; start an evidence manifest document (see template below).

Evidence manifest (template fields)
-----------------------------------
- Incident ID
- Custodian (name, email)
- Source system (IdP, API gateway, runtime node, bucket path)
- Artifact description and identifier (log file name, time range, byte range, checksum)
- Extraction command used (copy exact CLI or API call)
- Hash (sha256)
- Time extracted (UTC)
- Storage path for evidence (immutable-bucket URI)
- Retention class and legal hold flag
- Sign-off (custodian signature)

Minimal-impact extraction recipes (examples)
-------------------------------------------
- IdP audit query (Okta example):
  - CLI/REST: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://okta.company/api/v1/logs?filter=eventType eq \"service_token.create\" and published gt \"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z\"" 
  - Save to file: jq '.' > idp-audit-<incident-id>.json
  - Hash: sha256sum idp-audit-<incident-id>.json

- Control plane audit store (S3-backed):
  - aws s3 cp s3://redwood-immutable-audits/<prefix> ./ && tar czf cp-audits-<incident-id>.tgz <prefix>
  - sha256sum cp-audits-<incident-id>.tgz
  - Note: Ensure the S3 read action is recorded in an extraction_event audit and stored alongside evidence manifest.

- Runtime node volatile state (if live memory required):
  1) Snapshot current process list and open sockets:
     - ps auxww > proc-<node>-<ts>.txt
     - ss -tunap > sockets-<node>-<ts>.txt
  2) If memory dump is necessary, coordinate with Legal; use vetted tooling (gcore / fmem) with guidance from Forensics team.

Chain-of-custody and custodial handoff protocol
------------------------------------------------
1. Forensic Custodian creates the evidence manifest and records preliminary extraction details.
2. Custodian computes SHA256 on each artifact and uploads signed manifest + artifacts to immutable evidence bucket (s3://redwood-evidence/immutable/<incident-id>/). Bucket policy restricts writes to security:evidence-role and denies deletes.
3. Custodian triggers a custody-transfer message in incident channel and posts manifest link; IC and Legal must acknowledge in-thread.
4. Any physical handoff (e.g., encrypted hard drive) requires a signed handoff form with two witnesses from Security and Legal.

Retention policy mapping and data residency considerations
-------------------------------------------------------
- Retention classes (examples):
  - safety-critical-evidence: 10 years (legal mandate)
  - standard-incident-evidence: 3 years
  - ephemeral-debug-collection: 90 days (delete after review)
- When artifacts contain cross-border PII or customer data, Legal & Privacy must approve retention > 90 days and specify storage region. If cross-border transfer is required, apply Data Transfer Impact Assessment (DTIA) and record approval in manifest.

Audit logging verification checklist
----------------------------------
- Confirm presence of these audit streams for impacted timeframe: IdP logs, API gateway logs, control-plane authorization logs, model-serving runtime audit, and storage access logs.
- Validate monotonically increasing sequence numbers or time-based hashes when supported.
- Where event integrity features exist (signed log chains), capture and record the public verification proof with the artifact.

RBAC remediation and attestations
--------------------------------
1. Disable implicated session tokens and rotate involved service keys as a containment step (avoid immediate deletion).
2. Conduct a swift entitlement review: list of principals with the same permission set, when the role was granted, and active session inventory.
3. For customer-impacting privileges, require App Owner and Security approval for any re-enablement.
4. Post-incident attestation: within 7 days, App Owner completes an access attestation form listing why privileges were granted, corrective actions taken, and evidence links. Store attestation in control plane (audit metadata).

Packaging compliance evidence for auditors
----------------------------------------
- Package contents: evidence manifest (signed), extracted artifacts (sha256 hashes), extraction_event audit, custody receipts, legal-hold approvals, DTIA if applicable, and an executive summary (one page).
- Format: a single signed archive (tar.gz) with a top-level manifest.json and a human-readable PDF summary.
- Delivery: use secure artifact exchange (SFTP with MFA or approved e-discovery portal). Document the delivery in related_pages.

Integration with Secure SDLC and release gating
-----------------------------------------------
- If privileged incident root cause traces to an approved runbook or automated release, update the release record with remediation notes and evidence bundle ID.
- For code or IaC changes that granted unintended privileges, require a hotfix PR with accompanying postmortem artifacts and a mandatory security review before merge.

Example incident workflow (condensed)
------------------------------------
1. 00:00 — Alert: abnormal role activation spike detected by authorization anomaly rule. IC declared high severity.
2. 00:05 — Forensic Custodian assigned; manifest created.
3. 00:20 — IdP and gateway extracts performed; artifacts uploaded to immutable bucket.
4. 00:50 — Custody transfer acknowledged by Legal; short-term deny policy applied to implicated role.
5. 24–72h — Deep forensics, cross-border review, and remediation plan executed.

SLOs and operational KPIs
------------------------
- Triage start (assignment of IC and custodians): <= 15 minutes for P1 privileged incidents.
- Initial artifact capture into immutable store: <= 2 hours.
- Custody acknowledgment: <= 4 hours.
- Evidence package prepared for external audit: <= 10 business days.

Common pitfalls and mitigations
-----------------------------
- Pitfall: Overzealous deletion of keys or logs. Mitigation: prefer disabling/rotating and preserve artifacts; consult Forensic Custodian and Legal before deletion.
- Pitfall: Extracting logs into ad-hoc developer buckets in different regions. Mitigation: enforce immutable evidence bucket policies and region constraints; use temporary encrypted staging only with approval.

Appendices
---------
Appendix A — Sample custody transfer note (to post in incident channel)
- "Evidence uploaded: s3://redwood-evidence/immutable/INC-2024-229/; manifest sha256=<hash>. Forensic Custodian: Anjali Desai. Legal acknowledged: Priya Raman. Do not delete artifacts."

Appendix B — Recommended retention mapping by artifact type
- Authorization logs (IdP, control plane): standard-incident-evidence (3y) or safety-critical if legal applies.
- Runtime traces & ephemeral memory: ephemeral-debug-collection (90d) unless legal hold elevates retention.
- Chain-of-custody forms and attestations: 7 years (to support long-tail litigation).

Appendix C — Quick reference commands
- Hash a file: sha256sum <file>
- Create signed manifest (example using GPG): gpg --output manifest.json.sig --sign manifest.json
- Upload evidence (AWS CLI): aws s3 cp manifest.json s3://redwood-evidence/immutable/<incident-id>/manifest.json --acl bucket-owner-full-control

References and related docs
--------------------------
- Secure release gates and RBAC audit playbooks (see product and eng-sre docs).
- Legal hold and cross-border retention policy (security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention).
- Central immutable audit bucket policy (audit-logging).
